The reason is analytic: g_FS is proportional to 1/Lambda, so g_L is proportional to 1/Lambda; G_mu nu does not change under a constant rescaling, and Lambda g_L is independent of Lambda. The value of Lambda therefore moves nothing at all. Only the convention moves anything: whether a Lambda g term is included in T, which the paper leaves unstated. The row says exactly this. It understates the case slightly, since the value is provably irrelevant, but it does not overstate it.

A minor caveat on the extent figure "154 against 576". Re-run, the G + Lambda g set runs to z = 0.6, which is the edge of the fine-grid window, so 576 is a count bounded by the window and is not the size of the region. The tree never quotes the extent (formation.py:231-237 and 427-432 were read), so nothing rests on it.

(3) g_R of (11) and w of (21). The source shows "The choice of the Riemannian metric is arbitrary" at line 2493. The vector field (21) in the U1 chart matches the script's wvec exactly. The source states the expectation that a suitable zeta and g_R "might ... remove such regions completely -- at least for the Morse spacetime M" (line 4858). The row's "Could, in principle ... not tested, not claimed by the tree" is accurate. The tree marks the evidence "qualitative only", lists zeta among its free functions, and keeps D24 nucleation OPEN.

(4) No measured constants. Confirmed by reading: the result is pure GR on specified metrics, with no experimental input.

Every exact claim the tree uses was re-run, and the script exits 0 with "ALL CHECKS: AGREE" (log at verify/data/2505.02210-ec-rerun.log). The remaining incompleteness is model freedom that the authors state themselves, not data they lacked.

These are precision notes, not grounds to refute the audit. If folded in, they would sharpen the Lambda row ("stated at source only for Fig. 11; the value is provably irrelevant by scale covariance") and mark 576 as bounded by the window. STANDS holds.

L03 p.1221 also states the CI depletion in H, C, N and O directly ('meteorites are depleted in noble gases and H, C, N, and O'), so H3 is now READ. L03 also names aqueous alteration and parent-body heterogeneity, the caveat the audit's KEPT item says goes unnamed.

(2) The attribution discrepancy STANDS against the read table. Over all 60 shared elements, the tree's CHONDRITE matches L03 within 0.5% on only 9 (F, Na, Si, S, Ca, Ga, Ag, Ce, Bi). The audit compared 39 elements and found 7. The conclusion is unchanged: the table is not L03. The tree's P is 1040 against L03's 920, and its As 18.5 ppm is about 10.7 times L03's 1.73. L03's Ta row, which the audit did not carry, reads 14.4 ppb against the tree's 10. That puts the craft factor at 6.26e4 under L03 (computed). The binder stays Ta and no verdict moves.

(3) LBP25 READ at source (arXiv:2502.10575, Table 4 p.70, text pp.29 and 33). Table 4 gives N 1965, SD 970 (49%), n 22, SE 206, 95% CI 428, quality D, -33% against P14. LBP25 P has the same split: 989+-89 with n 32 in Table 4, and 989+-63 from 24 analyses on p.33. The abstract says the CI 'abundances of Hg and N are now significantly lower'.

(4) This sharpens DATA-DEPENDENT and argues against any firmer grade. At LBP25's P the crossover is 2282 ppm. Every LBP25 band spans it, including the narrow ones: the SD band (995-2935), the text band (1518-2412), 2 SE (1553-2377) and the 95% CI (1537-2393). (a) L03 Table 3, weighted CI group means: H 21015, C 35180, N 2940+-20, O 458200, Na 5010, Mg 95870, Al 8500, Si 106500, P 920+-100, S 54100, Cl 704, K 530, Ca 9070, Fe 182800, Ni 10640, Zn 310, As 1.73+-0.06, Li 1.46. Every carried value is exact.

(c) LBP25 Table 4: N 1965+-970 (49%, quality D, -33% vs P14), P 989+-89 (n=32), As 1.75+-0.17.
(d) PON14 (pyrolite): N 0.295% +- 0.0885 at 2 sigma, P 985+-157.6, Ta 0.015+-0.003 ppm, As 1.74.
(e) MS95 (pyrolite): N '3.18 ppm' F2, P '1.08 ppm' 15%, Ta 13.6 ppb, As 1.85. The units anomaly is as printed.
The tree's As 18.5 ppm is exactly 10 x 1.85. The P-bound factors 10.305 to 12.097 (721 to 847 kg) and the N crossovers 2123, 2273, 2282 and 2400 recompute exactly. The LBP25 N-binder factor of 13.070 also recomputes. The rederive script re-runs with exit 0.

REFINEMENTS:
(1) The audit's +-970 vs +-447 split is not a relay error. Both figures are in LBP25 itself: Table 4 gives 1965+-970, and the text on p.29 says 'grand average N = 1965 +- 447 ppm'. P has the same split: Table 4 gives 989+-89 (n=32), and the text on p.33 says '989 +- 63 ppm from 24 analyses'. Under the fluctuation.py precedent this is an internal discrepancy in the source, recorded and not repaired. Even under +-447 the band (top 2412) spans LBP25's crossover of 2282.
(2) L03's N +-20 is the weighted variance of only two meteorite means (N_met = 2). Those are Alais, a single analysis at 2900, and Orgueil at 2948+-535 over n=5. Orgueil's own 2-sigma low, 1878, lies below the L03 crossover of 2123, which is 1.54 of Orgueil's sigma away. L03's P comes from one meteorite (N_met = 1, Orgueil only). So the audit's 'L03 2940+-20 does not span' is literally true but understates the case. The fragility of the binder label was visible in L03's own Table 3, not only in MS95, PON14 and LBP25. That strengthens the audit's point that the tree dropped the uncertainty.
(3) Row 1 says that with P binding the advantage is 146-185x against cosmic and 33-42x against crust. The lower bounds, 146 and 33, are the LBP25 N-binding case, not P binding. With P binding only, the ranges are 157.9-185.4x and 35.4-41.5x. Across all five compositions they are 146.2-185.4x and 32.8-41.5x. This is a wording slip; the verdict is unchanged.
(4) Row 3 says 'L03 Ta row not carried'. It is now READ: Ta = 0.0144+-0.0001 ppm (14.4 ppb), and LBP25 gives 14.9 ppb (p.38). The tree's 10 ppb matches none of L03, MS95, PON14 or LBP25. The craft factor is 6.26e4 under L03 and 6.05e4 under LBP25. Both lie inside the audit's range, and the binder stays Ta.
(5) M's hypothesis is answered with evidence on both sides. FOR: N moved -33%, LBP25 flags it 'significantly lower', and L03's N rested on 6 analyses from 2 meteorites, so it was incomplete in that sense. AGAINST: LBP25 says 'revised CI-chondrite abundances of non-volatile elements are similar to earlier estimates'. LBP25 reports Orgueil N spanning 800-8200 ppm over 20 analyses, and its lower value comes partly from screening: it excludes G71's high chromatographic values and two P05 extremes. audits.published_statement: Thm 1.2 (p. 11): 'For any choice of past-compact smooth tensor S_ab(x) and for any symmetric past-compact smooth function Xi(x,y), there exists unique past-compact solution (omega~_1, h~_ab) of the Cauchy problem for the linearised semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon equations [(1.8) with zero data on Sigma_-eps] for any time t in [0, infinity). For any nontrivial choice of the sources S_ab and Xi, the solution h~_ab grows exponentially in time, but it can be bounded from above by the conformal rescaling of the Minkowski metric using a universal factor H, i.e. h~_ab <= e^{-Ht} eta_ab.' Thm 4.14 (p. 53): 'For a_i in (-infinity, 4m^2) and for any choice of past-compact smooth source S supported in the future of Sigma_-eps, the equation phi + W_ret(phi) = S ... admits a unique smooth and past-compact solution phi, supported in the future of Sigma_-eps.' Prop. 2.4 (p. 19): 'Let h_ab in Gamma_pc(T*R^n (x)_s T*R^n). Then, there is exactly one vector field X~_a in Gamma_pc(T*R^n), which makes the trace-reversal h-bar_ab divergence-free.'

de Donder gauge is a complete gauge fixing for PAST-COMPACT gauge vectors on R^n (Prop. 2.4, Remark 2.6); the formula divides by n-2

I tried to refute the grade in both directions and could not. NARROWED stands.

What I read at source. A live alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries call worked this time; the auditor's calls had hit a quota. It returned pp. 1, 41, 48-53 and 57-62 of arXiv:2604.01047v1, and the held dump (md5 4bac4a94...83c6e) matches on every passage checked:
- **Hypothesis:** Thm 4.14 (p. 53) and Prop. 4.12 (p. 51) both require a_i in (-oo, 4m^2), an open interval.
- **TT value:** sec. 5.2 (p. 60) gives a1 = a2 = a = 4m^2, b0 = 0, b1 = 60/kappa.
- **Application:** p. 62 says "if b2 is chosen to be positive and large ... one of the zeros of F falls into the cat, hence in this case the existence of solutions is provided by Theorem 4.14".
- **Not a misprint:** p. 57 restates the strict inequality in the authors' own words: "if a1, a2 < 4m^2, the semiclassical equation (4.9) can be put in the form (4.23)". The open interval is deliberate. So the mismatch between hypothesis and application is real, not a misreading, a misprint or a restatement. This is evidence the auditor did not cite, and it strengthens the audit.

Could the closed interval rescue it? No. I checked that the proof itself fails at a = 4m^2, not just the wording. With rho = (1/16pi^2) sqrt(1-4m^2/M)/M, read at (4.5) p. 41 with the square root in the numerator:
- J is finite at 4m^2, and J' diverges like delta^-1/2.
- For a < 4m^2, the term (gamma-a)^2 J' diverges, as Lemma 4.13 says.
- At a = 4m^2, A' = -2 delta J + delta^2 J', which tends to 0 from below like -delta/(16 pi^2). That matches the auditor's -6.3e-9 at delta = 1e-6.
- A'' > 0, so A' < 0 on all of I. The tangent construction in Prop. 4.12 therefore needs b2 < 0.

My independent mpmath code (verify/refute/thm12_indep.py, substitution M = 4 + x^2, not the auditor's code) reproduces all of the following:
- A' < 0 at every sampled point of (-50, 4).
- f = A' + gamma A''/2 increases on a 400-point grid over (0, 4), and its sup tends to 1/(8 pi^2) = 0.0126651.
- G'' at gamma = 4 - 1e-8 is negative for b2 = 0.0127 and positive for b2 = 0.0126.

So b2* = 1/(8 pi^2) stands. Continuum monotonicity of f is still a grid check, as the auditor said.

A second argument the auditor did not give closes the physical TT case. With b0 = 0, F_TT/gamma = A(gamma) - b1 - b2 gamma. This is strictly decreasing for b2 >= 0, because A' < 0. So it has at most one nonzero root in I: only two zeros in D, as GMMPS themselves say. The direct route fails too, which leaves only Thm 4.14, outside its hypothesis.

Why not another grade:
- **Not STANDS:** the tree's line "unique past-compact solutions exist" (linstab.py:142) covers S and TT together. At source the proof covers S only (a = 2m^2/(6xi-1) < 4m^2, where Lemma 4.13 holds).
- **Not WRONG:** no ill-posed TT source is shown. A complex-conjugate root pair, which Prop. 4.10 allows, or another route might still work. That half is open, not refuted.
- **Not DATA-DEPENDENT:** no measured datum enters.
- **Not OPEN:** the S half and the gap were both checked here. NARROWED, holds on a narrower scope than used, is the accurate grade.

The dependent pin FLAT_EXTERIOR_INHERITS_GMMPS = False rests on the posing on all of R^4, which was read and confirmed; it is unaffected.

Minor points:
- The auditor's b2 = 120 alpha~^TT_4 is correctly labelled as their own comparison. It follows from dividing by -1/120 on p. 60.
- Thm 1.2 on p. 11 was not re-read live. The held dump carries it, and the grade does not turn on it.

audits.published_statement: Not read at source (see source.via). This is the standard Plummer (1911) model as galpy 1.12.0 restates it (PlummerPotential.py:18-20, 74, 156) and as re-derived here. Potential: Phi(r) = -GM/sqrt(r^2+a^2). Density: rho(r) = (3M/4 pi a^3)(1 + r^2/a^2)^(-5/2). Enclosed mass: M(<r) = M r^3/(r^2+a^2)^(3/2) = M (1 + a^2/r^2)^(-3/2). The fraction outside r is therefore 1 - (1 + (a/r)^2)^(-3/2), which matches linstab.py:548-551 exactly.
published_hypotheses: H1 Newtonian gravity: the mass is the flat-space Poisson source, rho = lap(Phi)/(4 pi G). This is Plummer's setting. The M(<r) relation needs nothing more than Gauss's law applied to the potential.
H2 The density is exactly the Plummer profile (equivalently, the potential is exactly -GM/sqrt(r^2+a^2)), spherically symmetric, with scale a > 0.

H3 Plummer's physical context, which the enclosed-mass relation does not need: a positive-mass, self-gravitating stellar system in equilibrium (the n = 5 polytrope, isotropic DF). The tree uses none of it.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (plummer-enclosed-mass, audit grade NARROWED)
verifiers.reason:
I could not refute the grade, but two parts of the evidence under it need correcting.

(1) SOURCE. The alphaXiv quota is back, and I read the source through a restatement. Tabatabaei, Baghram and Mashhoon, arXiv:2406.10990, p.3 eqs (1)-(4), cite Plummer 1911 (ref [12], MNRAS 71, 460-470) and state Phi = -GM/(r^2+b^2)^(1/2), rho = 3b^2M/(4 pi (r^2+b^2)^(5/2)) and M(<r) = M r^3/(r^2+b^2)^(3/2), "from the Poisson equation". The tree's formula 1-(1+(a/R_s)^2)^(-3/2) follows exactly. read_status should move from NAMED-NOT-READ to READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT (2406.10990); the 1911 paper itself remains NAMED-NOT-READ. The same paper's eq (16) adds something the audit lacked. For a different relativistic Plummer metric (isotropic, (1+phi)^4), the Misner-Sharp mass is M(<r) plus a GR term of order GM/(c^2 b). The literature itself therefore treats the GR enclosed mass as metric-dependent, not equal to the Newtonian M(<r). That supports the H1 scoping the audit found.

(2) COMPUTATION. I re-checked independently in sympy and mpmath at 40 digits (verify/refute/plummer_refute.py, exit 0). Every number the audit computed checks out:
- rho_E = e^{2U}(2 lap U - U'^2)/(8 pi)
- m_MS = (r e^{-U}/2)(2rU' - r^2 U'^2)
- MS(R_s+) = m f, to 2.5e-13 relative
- outside proper-volume mass = -m f
- MS fraction 1.49992e-8, which is f(1 - m/2R_s), -5.0e-5 relative
- specthm's float 1.499999968679e-8, printing 1.500e-08

(3) WHERE THE AUDIT OVERSTATES IN THE TREE'S FAVOUR. The grade_evidence says the deviation "is below the printed %.3e, so the value prints as 1.500e-08 either way". It also gives -5.0e-5 as the worst case. That holds only for the Misner-Sharp split the audit chose. The audit names the Eulerian proper-volume sense as checked, but it integrated only the outside piece. I integrated the inside as well. The strong-field core (U(0) = 0.9999) carries a proper-volume mass of -0.015701 rather than -0.02. The proper-volume fraction is therefore 1.9107e-8, +27.4% relative, which would print as 1.911e-08. A core-alone definition (no shell, with MS(R_s) compared against the ADM mass -m) gives 5.0e-5, which is 3334 times f, because field energy beyond R_s, of order m/2R_s, swamps (a/R_s)^2. So the GR "fraction of its mass outside R_s" depends on the definition by margins far above printed precision. That makes the scope drift stronger than the audit says, not weaker.

(4) WHY THE GRADE STILL STANDS. In context, the specthm sentence (:648-651) can be read as the Plummer source density's mass ("the Plummer density falls over the scale a ... linstab.py's formula"). Under that reading it is exact. But certify.py's own notion of mass is Misner-Sharp (certify.py:114-128, 360-382), so a GR reading is equally available, and the tree does not scope the sentence either way. The formula is exact under H1. It is applied, unscoped, to a strong-field exact metric where no single GR value exists. That is NARROWED, not WRONG: there is no contradiction, and the Poisson-source reading is exact. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT either, since no measured datum enters. What rests on it still stands, because f > 0 under every definition I computed (Newtonian, MS split, proper-volume, core-alone). P2 therefore fails for the exact potential, and D26's 'NOT claimed', specthm class C and R8 are untouched.

verifiers.reason:
RE-RUN. I copied the script to verify/rederive/plummer-enclosed-mass.py and ran it. It exits 0 with ALL CHECKS PASS, and every number matches what the audit reports: f = 1.4999999812500002e-8; specthm's float is 8.38e-9 relative off; the series residual is 2.19e-24; the Misner-Sharp (MS) mass outside the shell equals m f to 2.5e-13; the MS fraction is off by -m/2R_s, worst -5.0e-5; the Eulerian mass outside matches to 3.5e-13. ENCODING. Section (A) checks the theorem itself, not a toy version. It starts from Phi = -GM/sqrt(r^2+a^2), takes the flat Laplacian to get rho, integrates for M(<R), and checks Gauss's law. The identity check ends in an `or` that falls back to four sample points, so I ran the symbolic branch on its own. It gives exactly 0, so the pass does not depend on the fallback. I also confirmed the series coefficient 35/16 by hand.

VACUITY GUARD. I replaced H2 (the Plummer profile) with Hernquist -GM/(r+a), isochrone -GM/(a+sqrt(r^2+a^2)) and a point mass. At the script's test points the gap from the tree's formula is 0.23, 0.26 and 0.99, so the check fails for each, as it should. Section (D) is the case with H1 removed, and there the script does find a departure, so (D) is not vacuous either.

A CLAIM THAT DOES NOT HOLD (the grade survives it). The audit says the GR departure is 'f(1 - m/2R_s)', 'worst at -5.0e-5', 'below the printed %.3e, so the value prints as 1.500e-08 either way'. That is true only when the GR mass is the MS mass. The audit computed the Eulerian proper-volume mass outside R_s but never inside it. I computed the inside value (verify/rederive/eulerian_check.py; the sympy derivatives are exact). The proper-volume integral of rho_E e^{-3U} over r < R_s is -0.0157009937591, not -0.02. The strong-field core (U(0) = 0.9999, confirmed) weights it by roughly e^{-U}. As a cross-check of rho_E, the areal-radius integral of the same density reproduces m_MS(R_s-) = -0.02000099970 exactly, and outside it reproduces -m_MS(R_s+). The Eulerian proper-volume fraction is therefore 1.9107e-8. That is +27.4% relative to Plummer's f, and under %.3e it would print 1.911e-08, not 1.500e-08. So the audit's line 'it depends on which GR mass is meant' is correct, but its magnitude claims ('the size of the departure is now computed', 'below printed precision', 'prints as 1.500e-08 either way') hold for the MS definition only. Its claim that f > 0 in the proper-volume sense was asserted, not computed; it does hold, since both masses are negative and f = 1.91e-8 > 0.

GRADE. NARROWED stands, and if anything this strengthens it. Under H1, Newtonian or linearised (concentric/composite), the formula is exact. specthm applies it without scoping to certify's exact metric, where the departure depends on which mass is meant: -5e-5 for the MS mass, +27% for the Eulerian proper-volume mass. f > 0 under every definition, so P2 still fails for the exact potential, and D26's 'theorem NOT claimed', the class C statement and the R8 hypothesis stand as written. It is not WRONG, since there is no contradiction and the sign is unchanged. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, since no measured datum enters. H-REST: a body of rest mass M has energy >= Mc^2 in any inertial frame, with equality at rest (Einstein 1905, NAMED-NOT-READ).

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis is that the authors lacked data. The theorem contains no measured datum: energy conservation follows from a symmetry and E >= Mc^2 from Lorentz invariance, so no later measurement can move it. What came later is refinement of scope, not data: quantum inequalities (negative local energy density allowed, bounded when smeared) and QET (2008; a hardware demonstration is reported in arXiv:2301.02666). Both show the LOCAL reading 'a signal brings only its carrier's energy' is stronger than conservation implies. Both confirm the GLOBAL budget, E_A >= E_B (Hotta p.16). This later knowledge narrows the tree's wording and moves no number: the global floor, Mc^2 or 1.9975 Mc^2 (1.9977 with Q), still binds the total energy entering the isolated system. The magnitude of any QET-type local gain at payload scale is not computed here; the only figure read is a power-law decay with distance in a spin chain (Hotta p.40).
audits.grade_evidence: The theorem as published stands, and every re-derivation agrees. The global budget follows from the energy balance under H-TT, H-ISO and H-POS (z3 C5a and C5b valid). Every tree number reproduces exactly (C1, C2), and no datum moves it (1.4e-9). The grade is NARROWED because massform.py:445-448 and 452/2038 use the result on a larger class than it covers, without naming four things. (1) H-TT: C6 computes the failure of Noether energy without it, and C4 shows the floor is local-frame (a 7e-10 deficit at Earth). (2) H-POS: C5d is SAT without it and C5e UNSAT with it; Hotta p.16 gives the local case, and the positive-mass audit the classical DEC-failing case. (3) H-ISO: 'a signal carries energy only through its carrier' and 'a bit brings only its carrier's energy' are narrowed by QET, where the destination gains E_B from a message carrying no energy, paid by E_A >= E_B at the sender (Hotta pp.5, 16, 40). (4) The pair floor drops Q conservation, conservatively: 1.9975 stays a valid floor, and the least floor with Q is 1.9977 (C3), a tightness discrepancy that is not an error. Not WRONG: nothing refutes conservation and no tree number is contradicted. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum moves it. - Across all 16 subsets, the only sufficient set is all four together. The check is therefore non-vacuous and its hypotheses are minimal.

Is it the theorem or a toy?
- C5 is linear arithmetic over a balance equation that it assumes. It checks how the Mc^2 floor depends on positivity and on there being no store at the seat. It does not check conservation itself.
- C6 is the Noether energy of a Lagrangian with one degree of freedom, a toy of time-translation invariance.

The audit over-states its own evidence in two places. Neither changes the grade.
1. "The global Killing-vector form is therefore demonstrated by computation (C6)." C6 is not the Killing form. I supplied the missing finite check as C7 in sympy:
   - In Schwarzschild, xi = d_t satisfies nabla_(mu xi_nu) = 0.
   - In FRW with scale factor a(t) it does not: the spatial components are 2 a a' g_ii / a^2.
   - For symmetric T, T^{mu nu} nabla_mu xi_nu = T^{mu nu} nabla_(mu xi_nu), so the current T^{mu nu} xi_nu is conserved only when xi is a Killing vector.
   This confirms H-TT by computation in the GR setting, not only in the one-degree-of-freedom toy.
2. The grade evidence says "The global budget follows from the energy balance under H-TT, H-ISO and H-POS (z3 C5a and C5b valid)." H-TT and H-ISO are not encoded in C5; they sit inside the assumed balance equation. Also, the audit's list of hypotheses whose removal breaks the floor names only E_store = 0 and E_other >= 0. E_rad >= 0 and E_anti >= B mu are equally necessary (my vacuity guard). The S13 check of radiated >= 0 is therefore load-bearing, not incidental.

Other points:
- The C3 encoding is physically sound. The lightest positive particle with B = 0 is the positron. Fe-56 has the lowest atomic mass per nucleon, below Ni-62. The 0.2372 MeV per nucleon difference (Z m_e / A) times B gives the 2.544e-4. The L-budget check does not actually bind, since antineutrinos or neutrinos can carry any leftover lepton number.
- None of this contradicts a tree number or the audit's conclusion. The audit's quotations of the theorem and its sources were not re-read here, because alphaXiv and arXiv are unavailable to this stage as well.
- NARROWED is the grade the evidence supports. Every tree number reproduces, and no measured input moves the result. The tree's wording uses the theorem without naming the time-translation, positivity and isolation hypotheses that C5, C6 and C7 show it needs, and pair_floor_j leaves out charge conservation, which keeps it a valid floor but not the tightest one.

audits.published_statement: Abstract: 'When spacetime is curved and/or has boundaries, we argue that the bound should hold in regions small compared to the minimum local characteristic radius of curvature or the distance to any boundaries.' Sec. 4.1: 'Choose our sampling time to be: tau_0 = f r_m = f r_0 << r_c, with f << 1. Substitution into Eq. (50) yields r_0 <~ l_p/(2f^2) (51) ... any reasonable choice of f gives a value of r_0 which is not much larger than l_p. For example, for f ~= 0.01, r_0 <~ 10^4 l_p = 10^-31 m.' p.16: 'tau_0 = f a_0, where f << 1. Equation (68) then yields a_0 <~ (r_0/(8 f^4 l_p))^(1/3) l_p. (69) A reasonable choice of f is f ~= 0.01.' Sec. 5: 'Let r_m be the smallest of the length scales ... the smallest proper radius of curvature ... is r_c ~= 1/sqrt(R_max) >~ r_m', then 'tau_0 = f r_m << r_c, with f << 1', with worked examples 'for f ~= 0.01'. Sec. 4.5 (MTY Casimir plates): 'Take tau_0 = f s ... A reasonable choice of f in this case would seem to be f ~= 0.1.' Pfenning-Ford eq. 23: 'as an example, if we let alpha = 1/10, then Delta <= 10^2 v_b L_Planck.'
published_hypotheses: P1 The flat-space Ford-Roman QI is ARGUED ('we argue', abstract) to hold in curved and/or bounded spacetime when the sampling time is small against the minimum local proper radius of curvature or the distance to a boundary. The QI covers a massless minimally coupled scalar, an inertial (timelike GEODESIC) observer, a Lorentzian sampler and the coefficient 3/(32 pi^2).

P2 The geometric scale is r_m, the smallest local length scale, with r_c ~ 1/sqrt(R_max) >~ r_m in the orthonormal frame, and r_m/gamma for a boosted observer. It is not an arbitrary size of the object.
P3 The hypothesis is f << 1. The number is a choice: 0.01 in the curved-throat examples, 0.1 for the flat region between Casimir plates (Sec. 4.5). No derivation of 0.01 is given.
P4 The energy density is about constant over tau_0: a static observer at the throat ('such an observer is geodesic') or a boosted geodesic observer.

audits.lacked_data: In 1995 F&R had no proof that the flat QI holds in curved spacetime at short sampling times, so they chose f by judgement. Later work closed that gap in their favour to first order: Pfenning 1998, Fewster-Smith 2008 and Kontou-Olum 2014/15 give a correction of about f^2, which is 1e-4 at f = 0.01. That makes 0.01 a conservative choice. None of this changes the tree's conclusion from this entry. The crossing moves as f^-2 at any f, so the Planck-scale crossing is fragile at every sourced f (39.9 or 3989 l_P) and a dimensional identity at all f. Evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis here: the one gap the authors named was later closed in their favour, and nothing in the sampling practice turned out inaccurate. Evidence for a narrower claim: the authors varied 0.01 themselves (0.1 in Sec. 4.5, 1/10 in Ford's 1997 warp paper), so 'practice' describes one paper, not their body of work.
audits.grade_evidence: Read at source: F&R sample at tau_0 = f r_m with f << 1 and take f ~= 0.01 in every curved-throat example (eq 51, eq 69, Sec. 5.1). The tree's attribution is therefore supported for gr-qc/9510071, and its 3989 l_P reproduces exactly (3989.42 by sympy and by numeric root). It is NARROWED rather than STANDS on three named points. (i) The practice is not uniform: F&R Sec. 4.5 uses f ~= 0.1 and Pfenning-Ford use alpha = 1/10. (ii) F&R's scale is the minimum curvature radius r_m, while the tree uses the core radius a. In the tree's own core r_c/a computes as 0.82 to 2.0, which puts the figure at 997..5984 l_P. (iii) The 3989 silently includes 3/(32 pi^2), and 'four decades' is 4.000 from the f = 1 crossing but 2.989 from the 4.09 printed just before it; that is a wording discrepancy. Nothing is WRONG: there is no counterexample, and the conclusion the entry supports holds at every sourced f.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS, the site would need to do four things: cite gr-qc/9510071 Secs 4.1/5.1, name r_m or state the a -> r_m identification with its 0.82-2.0 factor, say the 3989 carries 3/(32 pi^2), and correct the decades wording. Borde's own abstract supports the audit's main narrowing: "there will be causality violations if the initial (or the final) surface is not connected, even when there is no topology change." So Theorem 1's antecedent is not topology change. Its conclusion constrains every non-product M, whatever its endpoints. Borde p.20 says Tipler had already obtained Theorem 3's product conclusion under stronger assumptions. Tipler is still NAMED-NOT-READ.

I re-ran the computations independently in my own sympy script, not the auditor's:
- C2: R_kk = G_kk at l=0 equals 2(-a a'' - 1)/a^2 for both null directions. This matches.
- C4: χ((S1xS2)xI # S1xS3 # 2CP2) = 0, with b1 1 -> 2 and b2 1 -> 3. So M is a Lorentzian cobordism with the same nontrivial manifold at both ends, it is not a product, and Theorem 1 forces a CTC. Meanwhile create.py:235-245 still returns "no topology change".

Read in create.py, the claim stands for the class the prose means: a non-degenerate metric family on a fixed manifold with r > 0, which makes M a product, and there the theorems impose nothing. It does not stand as formalised. The predicate keys on two endpoint booleans, and specthm.py:1666-1669 W-enlarge has hyps [], so the product / fixed-manifold / r > 0 hypotheses are unnamed. One caveat that does not change the grade. verifiers.reason:
The data claim holds, with one place where it is stated too broadly and one presumption. Neither moves the grade.

(1) data_at_publication is empty, and that is correct. No measured value enters the scope claim. The claim is about logic: Borde's Thms 1 and 3 conclude 'M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1]', and Tipler's Thm 5, as Borde restates it (lines 2936-2941), needs topology change as its antecedent. A fixed-manifold enlargement with r > 0 gives a product M, so the theorems are silent on it, whatever any datum says. So there is no value_then or value_now to check, and no moves_conclusion row.

(2) The quotes in lacked_data were READ at source and they match. Borde line 2904: 'the results are purely kinematical'. Hayward 9805019v3 p.4 (lines 311-317): collapse-formed black holes 'are not expected to have the right topology'; quantum-fluctuation or early-universe ones 'may well'. Hayward 0903.5438v1 lines 814-818: enlarged 'by beaming in negative energy'. Hochberg-Visser lines 22-23 and 60-62: two throats that coalesce in the static case. The script md5 is 3acbcda3c02a47fdcae5c994f2b6d187 as stated, and the rerun prints RE-DERIVATION OK, with C4/C5 including the vacuity guard.

(3) Where it is stated too broadly. lacked_data says 'The result is kinematic (Borde IX: purely kinematical)'. At line 2904 Borde says that only of Geroch's theorem and his own sec. IV generalisation (Thm 1). Thm 3 assumes null convergence/generic conditions. Borde (lines 66-68) says Tipler's results assume Einstein's equation 'with a source with non-negative energy density'. Energy conditions are exactly where M's missing-data hypothesis could bite, because quantum fields are measured to violate them pointwise. The correct statement: data could bear on the energy-condition hypotheses of Thm 3 and Tipler, but not on the silence claim, because Thm 3's conclusion is satisfied trivially by a product M and Tipler's antecedent fails on it. So M's hypothesis is still answered with evidence (no datum can move silence on a product M), but the answer should be keyed to the antecedent and conclusion structure, not to the blanket word 'kinematic'.

(4) The presumption. lacked_data says 'never been measured ("nobody has ever observed one")', and its only cited support is the tree's own sentence (create.py:119, 249, 361). That is DECLARED, not READ: no observational wormhole-search paper or bound was read. The datum decides whether the route has an object at all, not the silence claim, so the grade is untouched. It should be marked NAMED-NOT-READ / OPEN, not given as evidence.

Grade: NARROWED stands, on the code-predicate, hypothesis-naming and 'Permitted' overreach findings, which this lens does not dispute. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, since no datum enters the scope claim.

audits.name: Alcubierre warp metric: the shift vector gives T^{0i} != 0

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/0009013v1 (posted 5 Sep 2000) = M. Alcubierre, 'The warp drive: hyper-fast travel within general relativity', Class. Quantum Grav. 11 (1994) L73-L77; all 10 pages read (eqs. 1-19, Fig. 1)
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries(gr-qc/0009013), which returned every page of the paper

audits.published_statement: Metric (eq. 8): ds^2 = -dt^2 + (dx - v_s f(r_s) dt)^2 + dy^2 + dz^2. Lapse alpha = 1 (eq. 2), shift beta^x = -v_s(t) f(r_s(t)) (eq. 3), flat 3-metric (eq. 5), f the tanh top hat (eq. 6). Expansion theta = v_s (x - x_s)/r_s df/dr_s (eq. 12). Eulerian energy density T^{00} = G^{00}/8pi = -(1/8pi) v_s^2 rho^2/(4 r_s^2) (df/dr_s)^2 (eq. 19). The paper calls this 'everywhere negative', so WEC and DEC are violated, and says SEC is violated 'in a similar way' (p.8). The metric is globally hyperbolic. The paper calls it 'a propulsion mechanism based on such a local distortion of spacetime' (p.8). THE PAPER NEVER COMPUTES T^{0i}, G^{0i}, a momentum density or a momentum constraint. T^{00} is the only stress-energy component it states.
published_hypotheses: general relativity with G_{mu nu} = 8 pi T_{mu nu} (G = c = 1); stress-energy read off the Einstein tensor of the chosen metric
3+1 form with alpha = 1, gamma_ij = delta_ij, beta^x = -v_s f(r_s), beta^y = beta^z = 0
f is a smooth top hat with R > 0 and sigma > 0 (eq. 6); v_s(t) is arbitrary, superluminal allowed
energy density evaluated for Eulerian observers n^mu = (1, -beta^i)/alpha (eq. 18)
no claim about any metric other than eq. (8), and no claim about momentum density
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (attribution): 'The shift vector gives T^{0i} != 0' (phase1.py:255, also :63-64 and :408-409) is not stated in the source, which computes only T^{00} (eq. 19). The tree does not compute it either: alcubierre_is_propulsion() passes has_momentum_flux=True as an input (phase1.py:256). Re-derived here (C2a, C2b), it is TRUE for Alcubierre's metric. At (t,x,y,z)=(0,1,0.3,0.2) with sigma=8, R=v=1: Eulerian J = (5.71e-2, 1.39e-1, 9.25e-2) and coordinate T^{0i} = (5.41e-2, 1.39e-1, 9.25e-2).

ADDED and REFUTED (generalisation): the tree states two clauses for every shifted metric: 'it fails automatically for anything with a shift vector' (phase1.py:93-94) and 'impossible with a shift vector' (phase1.py:535). 'THE STATIC/DYNAMIC SPLIT IS EXACTLY THE TRANSITION/PROPULSION SPLIT' (phase1.py:96-97, :533-534) is built on them. Four vacuum counterexamples are computed here, all with G_{mu nu} = 0 and so T^{0i} = 0 in every frame: flat space with constant shift (C5a), Painleve-Gullstrand Schwarzschild (C5b), rotating flat coordinates (C5c), and Kerr in Boyer-Lindquist (C5d), whose shift g_{t phi} != 0 cannot be removed by any coordinate change. A non-vacuum counterexample: any unit-lapse flat-slice shift with curl curl beta = 0 (e.g. beta = grad Phi) has Eulerian J_i = 0 identically while rho_E != 0 (C6a, C6c, C6d; Rodal arXiv:2512.18008 Prop. 2, read).

WEAKENED TO UNNAMED (frame): D4 (i) 'T^{0i} = 0' (phase1.py:31, :226) names no frame, and T^{0i} is not invariant. Computed here: coordinate T^{0i} = J^i - rho_E beta^i (C6e). The three readings give different results. COORDINATE: every non-vacuum point with rho_E beta != 0 fails D4 (i), even where nothing flows for Eulerian observers. EULERIAN: the irrotational warp metric passes D4 (i) (C6d). INVARIANT (no observer sees T^{0i} = 0, i.e. Hawking-Ellis type IV): Alcubierre fails at all three sample points (C4), but not everywhere. Per arXiv:2512.18008 (read), a Type I annulus about 2 x 0.014 rho wide around the wall on the equatorial cut has a rest frame. The tree must name the frame as a hypothesis. For Alcubierre the verdict is the same in all three readings.

WEAKENED ('by construction'): 'Alcubierre's shift vector violates D4 by construction' (phase1.py:63-64). Computed (C6a): for alpha = 1 and flat slices, 8 pi J_i = -(1/2)(curl curl beta)_i exactly, for any time-dependent beta. Alcubierre's J != 0 follows from his particular shift having curl curl beta != 0 (C6b: (-2.87, -6.98, -4.65) at the C2 point), not from the presence of a shift.

NOT DRIFTED, RECORDED: Alcubierre's net Eulerian momentum vanishes. J_i is an exact flat divergence d_j(K_ij - delta_ij K) (C3a), and the box integral gives |net|/int|J| = 6.1e-6 (C3b). So the exclusion rests on D4 (i) alone, which is how specthm states it ('Alcubierre fails D4 (i)', specthm.py:1272-1280). D4 (ii)'s zero-net-momentum clause does not exclude it. Its 'no centre-of-mass motion' clause is not evaluated here.
CONSISTENT: the tree's label 'propulsion' (phase1.py:409) matches Alcubierre's own phrase 'a propulsion mechanism' (p.8). His sense is free fall in a distorted geometry, not reaction mass.

A non-vacuum moving irrotational shift has Eulerian J=0 everywhere (C6c, C6d; Rodal 2512.18008 Prop. 2). In the alpha=1 flat-slice class the exact criterion is curl curl beta = 0 (C6a). So the claim holds on a strictly smaller class than the tree uses: Alcubierre, and shifts with curl curl beta != 0, read in a named frame. Taken alone, the generalisation clause is WRONG as stated (counterexamples shown) and the Alcubierre clause STANDS (computed). verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (either direction) for gr-qc/0009013: Alcubierre warp metric, "the shift vector gives T^{0i} != 0"
verifiers.reason:
I could not refute the NARROWED grade in either direction.

SOURCE, read in full myself (alphaXiv get_paper_content, gr-qc/0009013v1, all 10 pages). Every quotation in the audit checks out against the source: lapse alpha=1 (eq. 2), beta^x=-v_s f(r_s) (eq. 3), flat 3-metric (eq. 5), tanh profile (eq. 6), metric (eq. 8), K_ij=(d_i beta_j + d_j beta_i)/2 (eq. 10), theta = v_s (x-x_s)/r_s df/dr_s (eq. 12), and n^mu = (1,-beta^i)/alpha (eq. 18). Eq. 19 is the only stress-energy component the paper states, and it calls it "everywhere negative". The source also has "In a similar way one can show that the strong energy condition is also violated", "globally hyperbolic" and "A propulsion mechanism based on such a local distortion of spacetime". Confirmed: the paper never computes T^{0i}, G^{0i} or a momentum constraint. The attribution drift is real.

RE-DERIVATION. I re-ran the auditor's script: 18/18 PASS, exit 0. Every number quoted in the audit matches the output: J, T^{0i}, the 6.09e-6 net ratio, curl curl beta = (-2.87, -6.98, -4.65), and 8 pi rho_E = 2.32. I also checked that the script is not tautological:
- C6a takes an Einstein tensor built from the full Ricci tensor of a metric with three arbitrary functions b_i(t,x,y,z). The curl-curl identity is computed, not assumed.
- C4's type-IV verdict rests on complex eigenpairs of G^mu_nu and on there being no eigenvector with negative norm.
- T^{0i} = J^i - rho_E beta^i follows directly from n^mu = (1,-beta).

PHASE1 LINES. The cited phase1 lines are correct: 31, 63-64, 93-94, 96, 255-256, 409 and 533-535.

LITERATURE. I read both papers myself.
- Rodal arXiv:2512.18008, Prop. 2 (p. 16-17): alpha=1, flat static slices and beta = -dPhi give G^{0^i^}=0 and Type I everywhere. Its p. 30 has Alcubierre Type IV along the whole axis, plus a Type I annulus of width ~2 Delta, Delta ~ 0.014 rho, at the wall on the equatorial cut.
- Fuchs et al. 2405.02709: p. 6 states M_ADM=0 for Alcubierre, p. 18 has "the same kind of momentum flow structure is also observed for an Alcubierre solution", and Table 1 gives Alcubierre 8.0 ns at 0.04c with R=15 m.
All of these match the audit.

AGAINST A GRADE OF STANDS. The canonical entry itself lists the generalisation ("impossible with a shift vector", phase1.py:535) as a hypothesis of the result as the tree uses it. The verdict "static/dynamic split IS exactly the transition/propulsion split" (phase1.py:96, :533-535) rests on it, and it is false. A new check of mine closes the one reading the audit left open. In the COORDINATE reading, the audit's non-vacuum counterexample does not apply, because T^{0i} = -rho_E beta^i there. My sympy check R1 takes Einstein-de Sitter dust on a tilted slicing t = T + e x. It has g_Tx = -e != 0, so a shift, and G^{TT} = 4/(3(T+ex)^2) != 0, so it is not vacuum. Yet G^{Tx} = G^{Ty} = G^{Tz} = 0 exactly. So the generalisation fails in all three readings, including for non-vacuum metrics.

AGAINST A GRADE OF WRONG. The tree's actual exclusion of Alcubierre (phase1.py:255, :409; specthm RT) is true. It holds in the coordinate, Eulerian and invariant readings, with type IV at the sample points (C2, C4).

INACCURACIES THAT DO NOT MOVE THE GRADE. They are recorded here as discrepancies, not as refutations.
(1) The audit says Kerr's shift g_{t phi} "cannot be removed by any coordinate change". As stated, that is false. A shift is gauge: zero-shift coordinates (Gaussian normal) exist locally for any spacetime. What cannot be removed is non-staticity: no coordinates are both time-independent and shift-free. My check R2 shows the same thing for Schwarzschild. In Lemaitre coordinates, which share the PG slicing, it has alpha=1 and beta=0, and G=0 is verified. So C5d is no stronger than C5b, though it is still a valid counterexample.
(2) The same imprecision comes in through restating Fuchs: "a light-ray delta-t test shows the shift cannot be removed". What that test shows to be invariant is the frame-dragging asymmetry, not the shift vector itself.
Both points cut further against the tree's clause, not in its favour. Since every metric has charts with a non-zero shift, "anything with a shift vector" is not a geometric class at all.
(3) The source's "everywhere negative" for eq. 19 is strictly "non-positive". The audit quotes it faithfully, and nothing turns on it.

What would change the grade is as the audit states.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: ran a copy of the audit's script myself, checked whether it encodes the published statement or a toy version of it, and ran vacuity guards with the hypotheses negated.
verifiers.reason:
RE-RUN. I ran a copy at verify/rederive/gr-qc_0009013.py. It gives 18/18 PASS and exit 0 in 19 s. Every printed number matches the audit: J = (5.71e-2, 1.39e-1, 9.25e-2), coordinate T^{0i} = (5.41e-2, 1.39e-1, 9.25e-2), net/abs = 6.09e-6, Kerr |Ric| = 1.36e-166, irrotational 8 pi rho_E = 2.3196, curl curl beta = (-2.87, -6.98, -4.65).

ENCODING. The script checks the published statement itself, not a toy version. The Einstein tensor is computed symbolically for the eq. (8) metric with a general profile F(t,x,y,z). C1a (Hamiltonian constraint) and C1d (G^{00} = G_nn) are symbolic identities. C1b (eq. 12) and C1c (eq. 19) are numerical at 30 digits, on 2 profiles x 3 points, with v = 3/2. That includes Alcubierre's tanh profile (eq. 6), with the right sign and the right 1/4 factor. They are point checks, not symbolic identities, but the 3 points are generic and so are adequate. C6a is a symbolic identity for an arbitrary time-dependent shift (b1, b2, b3)(t,x,y,z): 8 pi J_i = -(1/2)(curl curl beta)_i. The Type IV test in C4 is sound: an observer u sees no flux iff u is an eigenvector of T^a_b, and a complex eigenpair is Hawking-Ellis type IV. I checked the beta^phi formula for Kerr (-g^{0i}/g^{00}) and the formula T^{0i} = J^i - rho beta^i (from J^0 = 0 and S^{0nu} = 0); both are correct. phase1.py:242-256 confirms that has_momentum_flux=True is passed in as an input; it is not computed. specthm.py:1280 quotes 'fails D4 (i)'.

VACUITY GUARDS (verify/rederive/vacuity.py). V1: with a non-unit lapse alpha = 1 + exp(-r^2)/2, the C6a identity fails (8 pi J = 1.28 vs 1.44), while the alpha = 1 control holds exactly (V2). V3: eq. 19 with the coefficient doubled fails to match (-0.565 vs -0.2825). V4: the C4 classifier is not stuck on type IV. On the equatorial cut (x = 0) it finds Type I (a timelike eigenvector) for rho in [0.980, 1.035] and type IV elsewhere (69/81 points). This independently reproduces the Type I annulus around the wall that Rodal reports. My width is about 0.055 at sigma = 8, R = 1. That does not match the audit's 'about 2 x 0.014 rho', which presumably reflects Rodal's parameters; I did not check that figure. V5: near the axis, all 27 points are type IV, which agrees with Rodal. V6: with a constant profile, G = 0, so the C2 thresholds can fail when they should.

OVERSTATEMENTS IN THE AUDIT TEXT. Neither moves the grade.
(1) C5d and the drift line say Kerr's shift 'cannot be removed by any coordinate change'. That is false as stated. Gaussian-normal (synchronous) coordinates make any shift zero locally. What cannot be removed is non-staticity: no coordinates are stationary and also shift-free. The refutation does not need this anyway. Each vacuum example C5a-c already has T = 0 in every frame, which refutes 'anything with a shift vector' in every reading.
(2) The drift line says 'COORDINATE: every non-vacuum point with rho_E beta != 0 fails D4 (i)'. That is too strong. Coordinate T^{0i} = 0 iff J^i = rho_E beta^i. The script's own check C6e correctly limits the claim to points where J = 0.

GRADE. NARROWED is supported. The Alcubierre clause is computed, and it holds in the coordinate, Eulerian and invariant readings at the sample points. The generalisation 'impossible with a shift vector' and the exact static/dynamic = transition/propulsion split are refuted by vacuum counterexamples that I re-ran, and by the symbolic curl-curl criterion, which I confirmed is non-vacuous.

verifiers.lens: THE DATA CLAIM
verifiers.reason:
I re-read all 10 pages of gr-qc/0009013 at source through alphaXiv. The audit's empty data_at_publication is correct. No measured value enters any equation of the paper. The only numbers are the parameters chosen for the figure (sigma=8, R=v_s=1, p.5), and those are a choice, not data. Because the result is a closed-form GR computation on an assumed metric, no later datum can move eq. (12), eq. (19) or the T^{0i} computation. So there is no value_then/value_now pair to check, and there is no moves_conclusion. M's hypothesis is answered with evidence, not presumed. I re-ran the rederivation here: 18/18 PASS, exit 0, with the same numbers as the audit (J, coordinate T^{0i}, net ratio 6.09e-6, type IV eigenpairs, Kerr |Ric|=1.36e-166, irrotational 8pi rho_E=2.32). That shows the source's equations hold, and that the gap is in the tree's attribution and generalisation, not in data the source lacked.

Two imprecisions, neither of which moves the grade:
(1) lacked_data says 'the paper cites no data'. The paper does cite the Casimir effect (ref [4], DeWitt 1979, p.9), qualitatively, as evidence that quantum field theory permits negative energy density. It is not an input to any equation or to the T^{0i} claim.
(2) The later_literature row for 2405.02709 says the paper 'confirms shifted warp metrics generically carry momentum flux'. Checked at source, the paper shows only two things: a light-ray delay greater than zero for several shifted metrics (Table 1), and a momentum circulation in its own shell (p.18). It credits the Alcubierre pattern to its ref [11]. It does not show that momentum flux is generic to any shift, and the audit's own C6c/C6d contradicts 'generically'. The fair wording is 'extends, for these metrics'. That over-statement is in the tree's favour, which M's two-way rule flags.

The numbers checked at source are correct: Alcubierre delay 8.0 ns at 0.04c with R=15 m (Table 1), and 'Alcubierre metric and similar solutions have M_ADM = 0' (p.6). The NARROWED grade stands: the Alcubierre clause holds as computed here, and the 'anything with a shift vector' clause is refuted by the counterexamples computed here. audits.published_statement: Perlick (1010.3416) p.13-14: Jacobi equation 'nabla_K nabla_K Y_A = R(K, Y_A, K)' (9) on a Sachs basis 'g(E_A,E_B)=delta_AB, g(K,E_A)=0, nabla_K E_A = 0' (12); 'D satisfies the matrix Jacobi equation D'' = D R (16)', optical tidal matrix 'R = Phi00 I + (-Re psi0, Im psi0; Im psi0, Re psi0) (17)', 'Phi00 = -1/2 Ric(K,K), psi0 = -1/2 C(E1-iE2,K,E1-iE2,K) (18)'; 'det(D) has only isolated zeros. These are the caustic points.' p.16: Sachs equations 'rho' = -rho^2 - |sigma|^2 + Phi00 (25), sigma' = -sigma(rho+rho*) + psi0 (26). One sees that the Ricci curvature term Phi00 directly produces expansion (focusing) and that the conformal curvature term psi0 directly produces shear. However, as the shear appears in Equation (25), conformal curvature indirectly influences focusing.' Seitz-Schneider-Ehlers p.6: '(sqrt A)'' = [R - |sigma|^2] sqrt A (2.8a) ... The driving term R - |sigma|^2 is nonpositive: the Einstein field equation with an energy momentum-tensor of an ideal fluid yields a non-positive source of convergence R ... as long as one considers only the area and not the shape of a light beam, the actions of R and F are not distinguishable.' p.5: conjugate iff det D = 0; rank 1 = line segment. Gao-Wald p.7: 'd^2A/dlambda^2 = -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu (11), A|p=0, dA/dlambda|p=delta, q conjugate to p iff det A = 0 ... G''/G = -1/2[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b] (13)'.
published_hypotheses: H1 (geometry): an affinely parametrised NULL geodesic, tangent K exactly null in the spacetime metric (Perlick eq. 9-10; Gao-Wald eq. 10).
H2 (screen): a Sachs basis -- E_A ORTHONORMAL, orthogonal to K, PARALLEL-TRANSPORTED (Perlick eq. 12). Only on such a screen is tr R = -Ric(K,K) and the trace-free part pure Weyl.
H3 (vertex initial data): D(0)=0, D'(0)=1; a conjugate point is det D = 0 (rank 1: line focus; rank 0: focus).
H4 (Ricci <-> matter): 'vacuum => trace zero' and 'sign R_kk = sign T_kk' use the Einstein equation R_kk = 8 pi T_kk; Ricci FOCUSING needs the null energy condition (Gao-Wald eq. 2; SSE p.6).

H5 (Weyl): psi0 enters the shear equation linearly and the area/expansion equation only through |sigma|^2 >= 0, so its effect on AREA is second order and sign-blind (Perlick 25-26; SSE 2.8a); its effect on SHAPE is first order (eigenvalues +-|psi0|).
H6 (smoothness): T continuous along the ray (SSE p.5); delta-type sources allowed in the lens approximation (SSE 4.25-4.26).
H7 (geometric optics): high-frequency limit of Maxwell on a curved background (Perlick p.4).
hypothesis_drift: DRIFT 1 -- H1/H4 dropped at nonlinear order (concentric.py:183-188 trace_ratio; composite.py:229-235 'Traceless in vacuum'). The tree's metric -(1+2Phi)dt^2+(1-2Phi)dx^2 is not an exact vacuum solution even where lap Phi = 0, so 'Vacuum forces the trace to zero' holds only to linear order in Phi. trace_ratio probes with k=(1,1,0,0), which is null in eta but NOT in g (g(k,k) = -4Phi), and with coordinate screen vectors. That probe cancels the O(Phi^2) residue to 3.3e-5, so the reported 7.55e-4 is the LINEAR density term 2 lap Phi (linear 8.00e-4; sympy-exact with the tree's vectors 7.64e-4). With an exactly null K and an orthonormal screen (the vectors survey() integrates with), |tr|/max = 7.32e-3 at a = 0.02. That is dominated by the metric's own O(Phi) residue: 6.52e-3 = 1.3 m/b at a point core, where lap Phi = 0. The verdict 'traceless to 7.5e-4' (concentric.py:356-359) reads correctly as the linear-order density. It does not describe the trace of the tidal matrix the Jacobi loop integrates, which is O(Phi), about 0.7 % -- the linearisation floor the report names at concentric.py:368.

DRIFT 2 -- sign of the tidal term (composite.py:229-235 tidal(); concentric.py:204-210 acc = -T A). composite.tidal returns T = -R_{kikj} = -K (sympy: T_code + K = 0 at linear order), and the loop integrates A'' = -TA = +KA. The source form is A'' = -KA (MTW 11.10; Gao-Wald eq. 11; Perlick eq. 16 with R = -K). Shown numerically. (i) Inside positive density composite.tidal gives tr T = -5.425e-3, so the loop DEFOCUSES where the null energy condition demands focusing. (ii) For a point mass M > 0 the code converges the RADIAL direction, where the physics (thin lens; arXiv:2409.06281 Fig. 3) converges the AZIMUTHAL one. The flip is immaterial for a traceless K because the eigen-directions swap. Measured in-process with the tree's own pipeline at m = 5e-3: 228.48 as written against 228.60 with the MTW sign. At m = 3e-3: no seat under either sign. It reverses the Ricci term. concentric.py:99-101 states the physics correctly using |trace| only, and no reported result rests on a Ricci-dominated integration. Recorded, not repaired.

DRIFT 3 -- H5 recast as a scaling claim (concentric.py:6-7 'Weyl focusing is quadratic in the source'; composite.py:25, 55 'Both signs seat ... because the focusing is quadratic'). The source makes Weyl's effect on AREA second order: confirmed, 1 - detA/lambda^2 = O(m^2) and the same for +-m. The conjugate point is set by the FIRST-order astigmatic focal length f = b^2/4|m|, which the tree prints itself (concentric.py:71-75). The converging eigen-direction moves linearly in |m|. Seating is sign-blind because the vacuum tidal matrix is traceless, not because the effect is quadratic. A discrepancy of attribution, not a refutation.

DRIFT 4 -- H2 nearly kept (concentric.py:198, 215-220). The screen starts as coordinate vectors of norm 1 - 8e-6 and is carried by Euler parallel transport. The departures are O(Phi(x0)) and O(h) and immaterial to det A = 0.

NOT A DRIFT -- 'THE SHELL DELAYS BUT DOES NOT FOCUS' (concentric.py:57-60). Exact: inside r < R_s every tidal component vanishes, linear and exact (sympy). Ray-inside-shell is checked by the tree (concentric.py:301-302).

audits.lacked_data: The Jacobi equation and the Sachs/Raychaudhuri equations are theorems of Lorentzian geometry with no measured input, so nothing Sachs (1961) or Raychaudhuri (1955) lacked can move them. The only physical link is Einstein's equation (Ricci = 8 pi T). The tree's negative-energy reading ('R_kk < 0 => defocusing') follows from that link for either sign of T_kk without any observation of negative energy. audits.name: Generating function for normal-ordered moments of a single-mode Gaussian (squeezed coherent) state, as used at research/warp-drive/fluctuation.py:27-31, 245-251, 279-292

source.located: The tree cites no source. The formula is the normally ordered characteristic function of a Gaussian state, chi_N(lam) = Tr[rho e^{lam a+} e^{-lam* a}], with (lam, -lam*) continued to independent (s, t). Its classical origin is Glauber 1963 / Cahill-Glauber 1969, not on arXiv. Read at source this stage: the definition of a Gaussian state (Weedbrook et al. arXiv:1110.3234 v1 eq. 19; Ferraro-Olivares-Paris arXiv:quant-ph/0503237 v1 eq. 2.4 and the general single-mode form 2.15-2.16; Brask arXiv:2102.05748 v2 Sec. II.5); the normal ordering D(alpha) = e^{alpha a+} e^{-|alpha|^2/2} e^{-alpha* a} (FOP eq. 1.48; Kuo-Ford gr-qc/9304008 eq. 3.10); the KF state and convention |alpha,zeta> = D(alpha)S(zeta)|0>, S(zeta) = exp[(zeta* a^2 - zeta a+^2)/2], S+ a S = a cosh r - a+ e^{i delta} sinh r (KF 3.9, 3.11, 3.16, from the banked full text d67/src/casmag/all/gr-qc_9304008v1.txt, md5 f1a6628604751cf61b2a4bd411b00153; the same convention appears at Brask eqs. 45-46).
source.via: No page read prints the exact formula <e^{s a+} e^{t a}> = exp(s a* + t a + N s t + M* s^2/2 + M t^2/2). Its defining ingredients were READ, and the formula is established here by symbolic derivation from them (check A) and by exact Fock-space computation (checks B, D). Glauber 1963 and Cahill-Glauber 1969 remain NAMED-NOT-READ.

audits.published_statement: READ (Weedbrook 1110.3234 eq. 19): Gaussian states are 'bosonic states whose Wigner representation (chi or W) is Gaussian, i.e. chi(xi) = exp[-1/2 xi^T (Omega V Omega^T) xi - i (Omega xbar)^T xi]'. READ (FOP quant-ph/0503237 eq. 1.48): 'D(alpha) = e^{alpha a+} e^{-1/2 |alpha|^2} e^{-alpha* a}'. DERIVED here from these two (check A): chi_N(lam) = <e^{lam a+} e^{-lam* a}> = chi_W(lam) e^{|lam|^2/2} = exp(lam a* - lam* a - N lam lam* + M* lam^2/2 + M lam*^2/2). At s = lam, t = -lam* this is exactly the tree's exp(s a* + t a + N s t + M* s^2/2 + M t^2/2) (fluctuation.py:28-29, 246), with N = <a+a> - |a|^2 and M = <aa> - a^2.
published_hypotheses: H1 one bosonic mode, [a, a+] = 1 (Weedbrook eq. 1; Brask eq. 2)

H2 the state is GAUSSIAN: its symmetric characteristic function is Gaussian, so cumulants stop at second order (Weedbrook eq. 19; FOP eq. 2.4). Mixed states are allowed; the general single-mode form is D S nu_th S+ D+ (FOP 2.15)
H3 N = <a+a> - |<a>|^2 is real and M = <aa> - <a>^2 is complex, with |M|^2 <= N(N+1) for a physical state
H4 the continuation to independent complex (s, t) is a statement about the coefficients <a+^m a^n>/(m! n!) of a power series; the right-hand side is entire
H5 for the KF squeezed coherent state D(alpha)S(zeta)|0> with zeta = r e^{i delta} and convention KF (3.11)/(3.16): N = sinh^2 r and M = -e^{i delta} sinh r cosh r, neither depending on alpha
hypothesis_drift: UNNAMED, NOT A FAULT, fluctuation.py:282-283: the code passes M = -w s c and Mc = -s c / w with w an unconstrained symbol. Mc equals conj(M) only when |w| = 1, and z3 check G proves this in both directions. The tree is right because w = e^{i delta}, but it never states unit modulus. The same holds for g at fluctuation.py:285 (needs |g| = 1 and real S_mod), and for the C(u) = (u+1/u)/2 cosine forms in kf318/kf319 at fluctuation.py:287-291.

NARROWER USE, NOT A DRIFT, fluctuation.py:27-29 vs 279-292: the docstring says 'single-mode Gaussian states', which includes mixed states; the code applies the formula only to pure D(alpha)S(zeta)|0>. Check D shows the formula holds on a mixed Gaussian, so the wording does not over-reach.

LOAD-BEARING HYPOTHESIS, RESPECTED: Gaussianity (H2). Check E shows the formula, given the state's own N and M, produces wrong fourth moments on Fock |1> and on vac+2. The tree does not use it there; vac+2 is computed by exact Fock matrices (fluctuation.py:265-272).
H4 is met by how the code uses the formula: gauss() takes only derivatives at S = T = 0 (fluctuation.py:248-250), so a formal power-series identity is all it needs.

DISCREPANCY IN THE TREE'S SELF-DESCRIPTION, recorded and not repaired: fluctuation.py:30-31 says 'numeric Fock series at 60 digits', but the code sets mpm.mp.dps = 50 (fluctuation.py:460) and compares after complex()/float conversion at a 1e-12 relative tolerance (fluctuation.py:481-483). The control is therefore effectively double precision. This does not affect the result.

SCOPE OF THE TREE'S OWN CONTROL: the Fock-series control (fluctuation.py:458-485) is taken at alpha = 0 at a single point. The displaced (alpha != 0) part of the formula, which feeds KF (3.18)/(3.19), is controlled in the tree only through the coherent limit (fluctuation.py:455-456). Check B closes this gap: 25 moments at 3 displaced squeezed points agree to 1.7e-14.

Its moments come out as <a> = alpha, <a+a> = N + |alpha|^2, <aa> = M + alpha^2, and at zero mean the Isserlis value <a+^2 a^2> = 2N^2 + |M|^2. verifiers.reason:
I copied the script to verify/rederive/g.py and ran it. It reproduces exactly what the audit reports: ALL CHECKS PASS, B worst error 1.69e-14, D worst error 3.77e-15, the E counterexamples (0 vs 2, and 0.019802 vs 0.020390), and z3 G unsat in both directions. I read the tree's line citations at source and they are correct: line 30 says '60 digits' while line 460 sets dps = 50; gauss() is at lines 245-246; M = -w s c and Mc = -s c / w are at lines 282-283; sub with sqrt(g) is at line 285; the 1e-12 tolerance is at line 483. The code matches the formula the audit attributes to it.

ENCODING. Check A is close to a restatement: the audit writes the Gaussian log characteristic function in complex form by hand (cumulants stop at second order), and does not check it symbolically against Weedbrook eq. 19's Omega V Omega^T quadrature form. A shows consistency, not independent proof. The load-bearing evidence is B and D, which use exact Fock matrices and truncated expm of the KF (3.10)/(3.11) generators without the transformation identities. That tests the theorem itself, not a toy: the higher moments are constrained by the state's own first and second moments.

VACUITY GUARD (verify/rederive/vacuity.py). I ran six mutants of the generating function against exact Fock moments with m, n <= 6, on 4 pure displaced squeezed states (r up to 1.1) and 2 mixed ones (nbar 0.4 and 1.3). The mutants were: M and Mc swapped, the sign of M flipped, the antinormal N+1, the symmetric N+1/2, M dropped, and M without the 1/2. Every mutant fails by between 3 and 3.8e3 relative error, so B and D discriminate. On the tree's own formula the one apparent residual, 5.12e-9, was truncation: on the nbar = 1.3 mixed state, raising D from 200 to 320 brings it to 3.07e-15. With the analytic KF-convention N = (nbar+1/2)cosh 2r - 1/2 and M = -(nbar+1/2) e^{i delta} sinh 2r, the error is 3.07e-15. At r = 1.1 and D = 300, analytic N = sinh^2 r and M = -e^{i delta} sinh r cosh r give 2.33e-14. This extends check C to larger r and to a mixed state. E is a proper negated-hypothesis test of Gaussianity.

ONE OVER-STATEMENT IN THE AUDIT'S EVIDENCE (it does not change the grade). Check F is vacuous as evidence for the formula's specific coefficients. All six wrong generating functions also satisfy <:T00^2:> = 3<:T00:>^2 identically. The reason is that :T00: = -K :(z^{1/2} a - z^{-1/2} a+)^2: is the normal-ordered square of a single linear form. So at zero mean, the single-variable Isserlis identity <:X^4:> = 3<:X^2:>^2 holds for any Gaussian (quadratic-exponent) functional, whatever N and M are. F confirms the tree's derived claim, and shows that claim rests only on Gaussianity, zero mean and the square structure of T00. It should not be listed as support for the generating function itself, which grade_evidence partly does.

The audit's other recorded items survive as stated: the unnamed |w| = |g| = 1 presupposition, the 60-vs-50-digit description discrepancy, and the alpha = 0 scope of the tree's own control. STANDS is supported.

audits.name: Wick's theorem for zero-mean quasifree (Gaussian) states

source.located: Wick, Phys. Rev. 80, 268 (1950), and its quasifree generalisation. Neither has an arXiv copy, so both were read through three restatements. (1) Kuo & Ford, gr-qc/9304008 v1, Sec. III.C pp. 10-11, eqs. (3.36)-(3.40): the exact form the tree inherits. (2) Hollands & Wald, gr-qc/0103074: p. 9 eq. (3), the quasi-free definition; p. 11 eqs. (6)-(8), normal ordering with respect to a quasi-free reference state, with Wick's theorem as the product rule (7); p. 9 and p. 14 eq. (17), where coincident Wick powers are taken only in quasi-free states 'of global Hadamard type'. (3) Pires, arXiv:1208.3651, eqs. (7), (11)-(13), (21), (24): the finite-temperature (MIXED-state) Wick theorem for e^{-beta K} with K quadratic, which restates Gaudin, Nucl. Phys. 15, 89 (1960).

audits.published_statement: Kuo & Ford (gr-qc/9304008 pp. 10-11): 'Recall that Wick's theorem applies to any quantum state |psi> for which there is a decomposition of the field operator into positive and negative frequency parts, phi = phi+ + phi-, so that phi+|psi> = <psi|phi- = 0. Both the Minkowski and Casimir vacua satisfy this condition.' Their (3.39): <:phi1 phi2 phi3 phi4:>_C = <:phi1 phi2:><:phi3 phi4:> + <:phi1 phi3:><:phi2 phi4:> + <:phi1 phi4:><:phi2 phi3:>. Their (3.40): <:T00^2:>_C = <:T00:>_C^2 + (1/2)[<:phidot^2:>^2 + <:phi_x^2:>^2 + <:phi_y^2:>^2 + <:phi_z^2:>^2], which keeps the diagonal terms only. Hollands & Wald (gr-qc/0103074 p. 9, p. 11): 'A quasi-free state is by definition one which satisfies w(e^{i phi(f)}) = e^{-w(f,f)/2}' (3); ':phi(x1)...phi(xn):_w = d^n/(i^n df...) exp[w(f,f)/2 + i phi(f)]|_{f=0}' (6); the product rule (7) 'is just a re-formulation of Wick's theorem'. Pires (1208.3651): for D = e^{-beta K}/Tr with K quadratic (7), 'the ensemble average is equal to the sum over all possible contracted terms' (11), e.g. Tr{abcdD} = Tr{abD}Tr{cdD} + Tr{acD}Tr{bdD} + Tr{adD}Tr{bcD} (24).
published_hypotheses: W1 (Kuo & Ford) phi+|psi> = <psi|phi- = 0: a PURE, vacuum-like (Bogoliubov-vacuum) state. They name the Minkowski and Casimir vacua.
W2 (Hollands & Wald) the state is quasi-free, w(e^{i phi(f)}) = e^{-w(f,f)/2}. Every n-point function then follows from the two-point function, and the odd ones vanish (zero mean).
W3 (Hollands & Wald) normal ordering is taken with respect to a quasi-free reference state w0 (Kuo & Ford: the Minkowski vacuum).

W4 (Hollands & Wald p. 9, p. 14 eq. 17) coincident Wick powers are taken in quasi-free states of global Hadamard type, so w - w0 is smooth and coincidence limits exist. Kuo & Ford's version is G_R = G - G_0 (3.26), (3.35).
W5 (Pires/Gaudin) a MIXED state with density operator e^{-beta K}, K quadratic with no linear term. This covers thermal states and Bogoliubov-transformed thermal states.
W6 a free (linear) field. The stress-tensor form is a separate input: Kuo & Ford use the massless minimally coupled scalar in flat space, T00 = (1/2)(phidot^2 + |grad phi|^2).
hypothesis_drift: BROADENED, VALID: pure to mixed. fluctuation.py:91-92 applies the formula to 'ANY zero-mean quasifree (Gaussian) state -- squeezed vacua, the Casimir vacuum, thermal states'. Kuo & Ford's condition W1 covers only pure vacuum-like states, and the thermal state is mixed. W2-W3 (Hollands & Wald, READ) and W5 (Pires READ, Gaudin NAMED-NOT-READ) do cover it. Computed here: A0-A2, B1-B2, C1-C3. The tree cites no source for this extension, but the extension is correct.

GENERALISED, VALID: off-diagonal terms. fluctuation.py:94 and the code at fluctuation.py:317 sum all 16 entries G_AB^2. Kuo & Ford (3.40) keeps only the four diagonal G_AA^2, which is exact for their periodic-z Casimir example because G is diagonal there. The tree's form is the general one, confirmed by A1 and by B2/B3 (off-diagonal and indefinite G). Kuo & Ford (3.40) is a special case, not a misprint.

DROPPED (unnamed): W4, the Hadamard / finite-coincidence-limit hypothesis. fluctuation.py:91 says 'ANY zero-mean quasifree' state. Hollands & Wald take coincident Wick powers only in quasi-free Hadamard-type states. If W - W_Minkowski is not C^2 at the point (a non-Hadamard quasifree state, or the Dirichlet-plate Casimir state at a plate), then G_AB, rho and <:T00^2:> do not exist, and neither the identity nor T1 says anything there. This limits the domain; it is not a counterexample. Every state the tree evaluates has a smooth G at the point.

WEAKENED at a dependent site: W6, the field model. The four-component form rho = (1/2) tr G is specific to the massless minimally coupled 4D flat scalar, which fluctuation.py:15-17 and noise.py:63-64 state. ledger.py:562-564 (D22) says 'Delta' >= 1/2, Delta >= 1/3 for every zero-mean Gaussian state' without naming the field model in that clause. With a mass term the same Wick identity holds over 5 components, but T1's floor drops to 2/5 (z3, D3-D4). With xi != 0, T00 is not a sum of squares and this form does not apply. Wick's theorem itself is field-generic, so this drift bears on T1 and D22, and it repeats the narrowing the sibling audit kuo-ford-1993-measure already recorded.

RETAINED: zero mean (fluctuation.py:91, :121-125), with the correct consequence that a displaced squeezed state has rho < 0 and Delta = 0. A4 (the extra term + m^T G m) and B4 (Fock 24.0500 against zero-mean Wick 24.6308) show the hypothesis matters. B5 (non-Gaussian |0>+eps|2>: 21.98 against 10.12) shows quasifreeness matters too.

RETAINED: flat spacetime with Minkowski-vacuum normal ordering (fluctuation.py:15-17). Perez & Sudarsky 2512.17789 (C29) show that in curved space the renormalised <TT> gains local curvature terms. The tree does not use the formula off flat space.

LINE SHIFT (bookkeeping, not drift): canonical.json gives fluctuation.py:70-80 and 279. The current lines are fluctuation.py:91-98 for the passage and 317 for the code; commits 477b721 and dbb3c9c added the DOCKET 67 correction paragraph above them.

A (sympy, symbolic symmetric 4x4 G, no positivity assumed): from Hollands & Wald (3)+(6), w(:e^{i phi}:_{w0}) = exp(-(w-w0)(f,f)/2). It follows that <:X_A^2 X_B^2:> = G_AA G_BB + 2 G_AB^2 for all A,B, and that (1/4) SUM = rho^2 + (1/2) SUM G_AB^2 exactly, which is fluctuation.py:94. C (sympy, exact): thermal <a+^2 a^2> = 2 nbar^2, plus a 400-term direct sum agreeing to 1e-100. D (z3/sympy): Delta' >= 1/2 for every symmetric 4x4 G (T1), with a vacuity guard; with 5 components 1/2 fails and 2/5 holds; thermal Delta' = 2/3, Delta = 2/5; a single plane-wave mode gives Delta = 2/3, i.e. <:T00^2:> = 3 rho^2.

later_literature.ref: S. Hollands & R. M. Wald, gr-qc/0103074 (CMP 223 (2001) 289)
later_literature.what: Gives the quasi-free definition (3) and state normal ordering (6), from which the tree's formula follows in one line (A0). Gives Wick's theorem as the product rule (7). Takes coincident Wick powers in quasi-free Hadamard states (p. 9, eq. 17); this is the source of W4, which the tree leaves unnamed. Also shows state normal ordering is not local and covariant (p. 20), so the tree's flat-space restriction is necessary.
Proves Wick factorisation for e^{-beta K}/Tr with K quadratic, anomalous terms included, extending Gaudin 1960. Its (24) is the exact 4-point factorisation the tree uses for the thermal state.

later_literature.ref: A. Perez & D. Sudarsky, arXiv:2512.17789 v2 (2026)
later_literature.what: Renormalises <T_ab T_cd> for Hadamard states via the OPE, independent of normal ordering. For any vacuum or squeezed vacuum in their 2D model, Delta T^2 = 2<T>^2 (20), i.e. Delta = 2/3, which is the tree's squeezed-vacuum value. They state it 'could have been naively anticipated from the Gaussian nature of such states as a general consequence of the Wick theorem ... the expectation remains correct after renormalization.' In curved space (C29) local curvature terms are added.

later_literature.ref: C. J. Fewster, L. H. Ford & T. A. Roman, arXiv:1004.0179
later_literature.what: Full distributions of SMEARED vacuum stress operators. Does not test the pointwise Wick identity; it is context for why the tree refuses the pointwise Delta as a demand row.

audits.lacked_data: Wick (1950) and Kuo & Ford (1993) lacked no datum: the result is a combinatorial identity of the free-field CCR algebra and takes no empirical input. Two things were missing, and both were mathematics, not data. First, a stated mixed-state form: Kuo & Ford's condition phi+|psi>=0 covers only pure states. Gaudin had already given the finite-temperature theorem in 1960 (restated in Pires 2012, READ). Second, a rigorous framework for coincident points: Brunetti-Fredenhagen-Koehler 1996 (NAMED-NOT-READ), Hollands & Wald 2001 (READ), and the OPE renormalisation of <TT> by Perez & Sudarsky 2025/26 (READ). Having this work does NOT change the conclusion the tree uses. It licenses the tree's extension to thermal states (computed in B1-B2 and C1-C3), and it confirms the squeezed-vacuum value Delta = 2/3 after renormalisation in 2D. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the identity is re-derived exactly from definitions (A0-A2) and verified at operator level to between 1e-13 and 1e-16. Evidence for it, in a weak sense only: the later framework makes explicit a hypothesis (Hadamard / finite coincidence limit) that neither Kuo & Ford nor the tree names.

(i) fluctuation.py:91 says 'ANY zero-mean quasifree' state, but the source framework (Hollands & Wald p. 9, eq. 17) needs Hadamard-type states, i.e. W - W_0 must be C^2 at the point. verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE
verifiers.reason:
The audit's facts all check out. I read gr-qc/9304008 pp. 1-19 and gr-qc/0103074 pp. 1, 3, 5, 8-11, 14, 16-17, 19-20, 22 and 35 at source through alphaXiv, and every quotation in the audit matches the page text. Kuo & Ford's condition phi+|psi> = <psi|phi- = 0 and their eqs. (3.39) and (3.40) appear exactly as quoted, and the Casimir example uses periodic z boundaries. Hollands & Wald's definitions (3), (6) and (7) and their 'global Hadamard type' sentence on p. 9 also match. The identity itself holds. A fresh Fock-space script, written separately from the audit's, takes a two-mode mixed state built as thermal, then two-mode squeezed, then beam-split. Its random complex mode functions give a G with off-diagonal entries up to 2.38 and an indefinite spectrum, and the mean is 0. Normal ordering is done by explicit reordering. At N=30 the script gives <:T00^2:> = 43.2598950 against rho^2 + (1/2) SUM G_AB^2 = 43.2599016, a relative residual of 1.5e-7. That fits truncation at N=30, given the audit's own convergence from 1.1e-9 at N=34 to 2e-13 at N=46. A 1.5e-7 residual does not by itself rule out a small real deviation; it only fits truncation. The script is at verify/refute/wick_indep.py. So the dispute is over the grade, not the facts, and the NARROWED rests on two grounds that do not hold up for this key.

(i) The W4 'Hadamard / finite-coincidence' hypothesis is not dropped. It is presupposed by the formula's own terms. fluctuation.py:94 defines G_AB = <:d_A phi d_B phi:>, and fluctuation.py:16 names the 'coincidence limit'. In flat space, normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum, the identity needs only that the coincidence limits of d d'(w - w0) exist at the point. Full global Hadamard is more than that: Hollands & Wald need it to build the extended algebra W(M,g) in curved spacetime, not for the Wick identity itself. Wherever G_AB exists, the point-split Wick expansion gives LHS = RHS. Wherever G_AB does not exist, neither side exists. The audit concedes this itself: the formula 'says nothing; it is not false there' and 'every state the tree evaluates has a smooth G'. So there is no state on which the tree's statement has content and fails, and therefore no 'smaller class' on which it holds. By this standard any equation would be NARROWED for not stating that its own terms exist. The board's sibling audit minkowski-wightman-wick was graded STANDS on this same shape: 'any real sampler' (noise.py:63) leaves its finiteness condition implicit, every sampler the tree evaluates meets it, and that was recorded as a discrepancy rather than a narrowing. Grading the two differently would over-represent, in favour of M's hypothesis, a gap that is only one of wording.

(ii) The field-model drift at ledger.py:562-564 (D22) is a drift in T1, not in Wick's theorem. The audit itself says 'Wick's theorem itself is field-generic', and that the drift 'repeats the narrowing the sibling audit kuo-ford-1993-measure already recorded'. That audit is graded NARROWED and names this drift explicitly ('massless' dropped, with the 5x5 floor at 2/5). Counting it again here moves one finding onto the wrong key. Even read as a T1 matter, D22 attributes T1 to fluctuation.py, whose header at :15-17 names the massless minimally coupled scalar, and the same D22 row says 'free minimal scalar in Minkowski'.

What remains is everything the rubric gives for STANDS. The statement and hypotheses as used are confirmed. The tree's two departures from Kuo & Ford are both valid generalisations: mixed states are licensed by H&W's quasi-free definition (3) and by Gaudin via Pires (the audit's reading), and the off-diagonal G terms are confirmed by A1/B2 and by my own check. The re-derivation agrees, 20/20 per the audit and independently above. The controls fail where they should: nonzero mean, and a non-Gaussian state. No datum enters, so none can move the conclusion.

Recommended record: STANDS, with two discrepancies noted and neither a refutation. First, the finite-coincidence-limit presupposition is unnamed at fluctuation.py:91. Second, the field-model clause belongs to kuo-ford-1993-measure. Nothing in this verification was repaired, and no file under research/ was touched.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION
verifiers.reason:
I re-ran the script from a copy at verify/rederive/wick-theorem-quasifree.py. It printed 20/20 PASS and exited 0 in 48 s. Its output matches the audit's recorded rederive/wick-theorem-quasifree.out line for line. The audit says the run takes 2-5 min; that is only an overestimate.

ENCODING. Part A is the theorem in algebraic form: Isserlis applied to the generating function exp(t^T G t/2), with G a general symbolic symmetric 4x4 matrix and no positivity assumed. A1, A2 and A4 are real symbolic identities. A0 is weaker than the audit presents it. It checks the Hollands & Wald link only for scalars w and w0, where it is trivially true. The step that carries the weight is that the f-derivatives of exp(-(w-w0)(f,f)/2) are Gaussian moments with covariance G = sym(w - w0). The script states that step in a comment and builds it in by choosing that generating function; it does not compute it. Part B is what checks the theorem independently, without assuming it. It works at operator level in Fock space, with normal ordering done by explicit creation-left reordering (bosonic parts commute, so the encoding is sound). It covers pure and mixed states, with diagonal, off-diagonal and indefinite G. B2's residual falls from 1.1e-9 at N=34 to 2e-13 at N=46, which shows it is truncation error. One limit: B is a two-mode toy in which the four observables X_A stand in for d_A phi; they are not field derivatives. Part A covers the mode-count independence symbolically, so the two parts together cover the theorem as the tree states it.

VACUITY. The script's own controls fail as they should: B4 (nonzero mean, rel 2.4e-2) and B5 (non-Gaussian pure state, rel 0.54). I added verify/rederive/vacuity_extra.py, which imports the audit's harness unchanged, to test the hypothesis the tree extends: mixed states. Every state in it has zero mean.
- V1, a mixture of two thermal states (mixed, not quasifree): rel 0.43, fails.
- V2, the Fock state |1,0>: rel 1.0, fails.
- V3, a mixture of +/- squeezed vacua: rel 0.85, fails.
- V4, a single squeezed vacuum at N=30 (quasifree), the positive control: rel 8e-14, holds.
So the check tells quasifree states from non-quasifree ones even among zero-mean mixed states. 'Mixed' alone is not enough; the tree's wording 'zero-mean quasifree' is the hypothesis that does the work, and the tree states it. D2 is a real vacuity guard for the z3 floor. D1 and D4 (Cauchy-Schwarz floors 1/2 at n=4 and 2/5 at n=5) agree with a hand check.

LINES. fluctuation.py:91 ('For ANY zero-mean quasifree'), :96 and :317 (T2 = rho^2 + SUM G^2/2), and ledger.py:562-564, all match the audit.

GRADE. NARROWED holds, but on one leg, not two. (i) The tree never names the Hadamard / finite-coincidence-limit precondition. Line 16 says 'coincidence limit', but nothing says the limit must exist. Under M's rule that every limitation is a NAMED hypothesis, this narrows the claim. It is arguably a well-definedness condition, since G_AB must exist for the formula to mean anything; it is a gap in the domain, not a counterexample. (ii) The D22 leg (ledger.py:562-564 omits the field model) is weaker than the audit presents it. The clause attributes T1 to fluctuation.py, which names the massless minimal scalar at :15-17, and the next sentence at :564 says 'For the free minimal scalar in Minkowski'. It is also a point about T1's wording, not about Wick's theorem; the audit itself calls Wick field-generic. I would record (ii) as a note on the dependent result T1, not as grounds for this grade. If (i) is read as a well-definedness condition rather than a dropped hypothesis, the evidence supports STANDS. Nothing in the re-run supports WRONG, DATA-DEPENDENT or OPEN.
